findings.label: Batch partial settlement asymmetry
findings.description: Batch validation is atomic (all-or-nothing on validation failure) but execution is sequential (partial settlement possible on mid-batch errors). Callers must handle recovery; no automatic rollback or retry. Clarify expectations in API docs and error reporting.

findings.label: Fee calculation nonce tracking unused
findings.description: Event emission hardcodes nonce values (0–8) instead of using incremented per-event-type counters. EventNonce struct is defined but never queried or incremented. Offline indexing may conflate events with colliding nonce values across event types.

findings.label: Escrow state machine lacks preimage validation detail
findings.description: Escrow with condition_hash compares BytesN<32> directly but doesn't specify hash algorithm or preimage format. Caller must hash the preimage before passing it to settle_escrow(). This works but is worth documenting or delegating hashing to the contract for better UX.

findings.label: Cross-border router TTL renewal deferred
findings.description: Route caching is implemented but TTL renewal on find_best_route() is not. Routes could expire mid-transaction if not accessed within 60 minutes. Acceptable for now as a known gap; route expiry is catchable and triggers re-submission.

findings.label: Compliance check not invoked in stellar-payments
findings.description: register_compliance_check() stores the contract address but no payment entrypoint actually calls it. Compliance hooks are registered but never used; settlement proceeds without checking. Compliance integration point exists but is non-functional in this iteration.

findings.label: Fee balance withdrawal lacks origin tracking
findings.description: withdraw_fees() allows admin to withdraw all fees for an asset without tracking which payments generated them. No audit trail of fee source. Acceptable for fees (fungible, not privacy-sensitive) but limits transparency.

findings.label: Initial fee recipient defaults to contract address
findings.description: When FeeConfig has no explicit fee_recipient, it defaults to the contract's own address. Fees can then only be withdrawn by the admin. This works but is non-obvious; document that fee_recipient must be explicitly set in config if a different address is desired.
